prompt.context_jp: 宮沢がマイクの前に立った瞬間——
prompt.prompt_jp: 役員たちの視線___一斉に宮沢へ集まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks this as a new, attention-grabbing event.

feedback.correct_en: The executives' gaze suddenly focusing on Miyazawa is a new event the narrator is reporting — が introduces it as fresh information at this moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 役員たちの視線 into an already-established topic being commented on, but here the shift of gaze itself is the news.

prompt.context_jp: 試作品を机に置こうとして——
prompt.prompt_jp: 持参した一足を机の中央に置く手___、わずかに震えていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that reveals the trembling hand as the newly noticed detail.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator zooms in on a specific detail — his hand trembling — as a new observation. が marks this fresh subject the reader hasn't been attending to.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 手 is already the established topic being contrasted; here it's a newly spotlighted subject.

contrast_examples.en: His hand (as for it) didn't tremble.

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が話し始めた場面の描写。
prompt.prompt_jp: 声___ゆっくりと、しかし芯のある調子で会議室に広がっていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that treats 'his voice' as the ongoing theme being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: The passage is characterizing his voice — already in the scene — telling us what it was like. は frames 声 as topic for comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the voice as newly appearing information, but the voice has just been established and is now being described.

contrast_examples.en: His voice was low (as a feature).

prompt.context_jp: 相手がアトランティスだと知って——
prompt.prompt_jp: 大地の顔から血の気___引いていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for a vivid, newly-unfolding physical reaction.

feedback.correct_en: 血の気が引く is a set event-description; が presents the color draining as a new, happening-now change.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would suggest 血の気 is a previously raised topic being compared with something else — not the case here.

contrast_examples.en: As for his temper, it's hot-blooded.

prompt.context_jp: 七時を過ぎて、沈黙の中——
prompt.prompt_jp: 机の上の電話___、ためらいがちに鳴った。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the long-awaited phone ringing as a new event.

feedback.correct_en: The whole room has been waiting for this phone to ring. The ringing is the event-of-the-moment, so が marks the newly-breaking subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the phone an already-topicalized thing being commented on, draining the sentence of its 'at last!' impact.

contrast_examples.en: The phone (as for it) didn't ring.

prompt.context_jp: 落選理由を宮沢が伝える場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: やっぱり うちのシューズ___ 過去に使用例がないってことだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'our shoes' as the topic the reason is being given about.

feedback.correct_en: うちのシューズ is the topic being characterized ('as for our shoes, there's no prior use'). は sets up what the explanation is about.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it a newly introduced subject, but the shoes are already the shared topic of the whole conversation.

contrast_examples.jp: うちのシューズは使用例がない。
contrast_examples.en: As for our shoes, there are no prior cases.

contrast_examples.jp: うちのシューズが選ばれた。

prompt.context_jp: 口にしてはみたものの——
prompt.prompt_jp: 負け___とうに覚悟していたはずなのに、口にすると胸の奥がずしりと重くなる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets 'defeat' against the actual reaction ('and yet').

feedback.correct_en: 負けは…のに creates a contrast: 'defeat, I'd been ready for — and yet…'. は carries this contrastive, 'as for X, however' nuance.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just mark 負け as the new subject of 覚悟する, losing the characteristic 'X was prepared for, but still…' contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 失敗は覚悟していたが、現実は重かった。
contrast_examples.en: Failure I was ready for, but reality was heavy.

prompt.context_jp: 富島が負けを予言する——
prompt.prompt_jp: 相手___業界最大手。利益度外視の低価格で来られたら うちは とてもかなわんよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that identifies who the opponent IS.

feedback.correct_en: 相手は〜 states what the opponent is (predicate nominal, topic–comment). This is the standard 'X is Y' pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively single out 相手 as 'it's the opponent who is the industry leader,' which doesn't match the flat statement of fact.

contrast_examples.en: The opponent is a big company.
It was the opponent (who) was the problem.

prompt.context_jp: 大橋への宮沢の宣言——
prompt.prompt_jp: こはぜ屋の現状___ 全て社長である私の責任なんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames 'Kohazeya's current state' as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: He's declaring responsibility about an already-shared subject (the company's situation). は sets it up as topic for his statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present the situation as newly introduced info, but it's exactly what the whole meeting has been about.

contrast_examples.en: Who will take responsibility? (new info focus)

prompt.context_jp: 古い試作品を指して——
prompt.prompt_jp: これ___ たすきです。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for an 'X is Y' identification statement.

feedback.correct_en: これはYです is the canonical 'this is Y' pattern — は topicalizes これ and the predicate identifies it.
feedback.incorrect_en: これがたすきです would mean 'THIS is the sash (as opposed to other things)' — exhaustive focus, which isn't what he's doing when solemnly naming it.

contrast_examples.en: THIS is the pen (identifying which one).

prompt.context_jp: 帰路の車内——
prompt.prompt_jp: 街路樹の合間から差す夕日___、車内をやわらかく染めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that paints a scene with the sunset as a newly observed element.

feedback.correct_en: Scene-setting descriptions of what's visible/happening in a moment typically use が — the sunset enters the scene as a new sensory detail.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the setting sun into an established topic being compared, which doesn't fit a fresh descriptive image.

prompt.context_jp: 短い返事でもその重みを噛みしめて——
prompt.prompt_jp: それでも、その一言の重さを彼___よく分かっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that puts the subject 'he' in topic/contrast position ('as for him…').

feedback.correct_en: 彼は contrasts with the easy-sounding one-word reply: 'the answer could be short — but HE knew its weight.' は carries that contrastive-topic reading.
feedback.incorrect_en: 彼が would exhaustively single him out ('it was he who understood'), which doesn't match the reflective, contrastive mood.

contrast_examples.jp: 簡単だが、彼は重さを知っていた。
contrast_examples.en: It's simple, but he knew its weight.

prompt.context_jp: プレゼンを終えて廊下で——
prompt.prompt_jp: 結果___どう転ぶかは分からない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks 'the result' as what the embedded question is about.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the embedded clause どう転ぶか, 結果 is the subject of 転ぶ, newly stated — が marks it. The outer は is on か自体 (結果がどう転ぶかは…).
feedback.incorrect_en: は on 結果 would try to topicalize it over the whole sentence, but the outer topic marker は is already attached after か, so 結果 needs が.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来るかは分からない。
彼は来るか分からない。
contrast_examples.en: As for him, I don't know if he'll come.

prompt.context_jp: 工場で働く者だけが持つ響き——
prompt.prompt_jp: 声には、工場で汗を流してきた者だけ___持つ確信が滲んでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 'only those who sweated in the factory' as the exhaustive bearer of the conviction.

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが持つ is a tight relative clause: the subject of 持つ is 'only those…', and が marks that exhaustive subject inside the clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a relative clause like this is unnatural; relative-clause subjects usually take が (or の).

prompt.context_jp: 電話を切った直後——
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰も声を掛けられない数秒___過ぎる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'a few seconds' as the newly-arising subject passing by.

feedback.correct_en: 数秒が過ぎる reports an event as it occurs — が introduces 数秒 as fresh subject in this narrative beat.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would require 数秒 to be an already-established topic, but here it's a moment-of-silence surfacing in the scene.

prompt.context_jp: プレゼン直前、宮沢の覚悟——
prompt.prompt_jp: この場を逃せば、こはぜ屋の未来はまた一段と___なる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits 'the future becomes even more precarious.'

feedback.correct_en: 未来が細くなる is an idiomatic metaphor meaning prospects/paths narrow — fitting a shrinking business future.
feedback.incorrect_en: 狭くなる is used for physical/space narrowing; 短くなる (shorten) and 低くなる (lower) don't collocate with 未来 in this metaphorical sense.

prompt.context_jp: 富島がつぶやく——
prompt.prompt_jp: 利益度外視の低価格で来られたら うちは とても___よ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'we can't possibly match them.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜にかなわない means 'cannot compete / is no match for.' かなわん is its blunt dialect/elderly-male form, fitting Tomijima's speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: いけん (= no good), ならん (= can't be allowed), つかん don't carry the 'can't compete with' meaning here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼には かなわない。

prompt.context_jp: 坂本が転勤を伝えなかった理由——
prompt.prompt_jp: 皆さんの やる気に ___じゃないかと 思いまして。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'dampen (someone's) motivation.'

feedback.correct_en: 水を差す is the fixed idiom for 'to pour cold water on / dampen enthusiasm' — exactly what Sakamoto feared doing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 水に流す = let bygones be bygones; 水を向ける = draw someone out in conversation; 水をかける = literal 'pour water on,' not idiomatic here.

contrast_examples.jp: 盛り上がりに水を差す。

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が思い切って一言——
prompt.prompt_jp: それ以上に ___言わしていただくと…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adverb for 'if I may presume to say so.'

feedback.correct_en: あえて言う = 'to go so far as to say' — the speaker acknowledges it's bold but says it anyway. Fits the moment he declares his claim.
feedback.incorrect_en: かえって = on the contrary; せめて = at least; どうせ = anyway/in any case — none capture the 'daring to say' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 坂本が黙って社を守っていた事実——
prompt.prompt_jp: 坂本が黙ってこはぜ屋を___続けていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'to shield / stand up for.'

feedback.correct_en: 庇う carries the specific nuance of taking flak for someone — Sakamoto absorbed the branch manager's pressure to protect Kohazeya.
feedback.incorrect_en: 守る (protect) is too generic and lacks the 'at personal cost' nuance; 隠す (hide) and 抱える (hold) don't fit the sentence meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が古い試作品を掲げて——
prompt.prompt_jp: これは、社員たちから託された___なんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word Miyazawa uses as a metaphor passed down between runners.

feedback.correct_en: たすき is the ekiden (relay) sash passed between runners — a culturally rich metaphor echoing the marathon-tabi theme and 'passing it on'.
feedback.incorrect_en: バトン fits track relays but misses the ekiden/traditional Japanese resonance; 旗 (flag) and 重荷 (burden) break the running-relay image.

prompt.context_jp: 富島とあけみが言い合いになり——
prompt.prompt_jp: 言い合いが___なくなりそうな空気を、宮沢が手のひらで制した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that fits 'threatening to become endless.'

feedback.correct_en: 際限がない is the set phrase for 'endless, without bounds' — exactly how a spiraling argument feels.
feedback.incorrect_en: 限界がない is unidiomatic in this sense; 程度 means 'degree'; 限度を超える exists but doesn't fit the ない pattern here.

prompt.context_jp: 大地が父にリストラの件で話を切り出す場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural coming from Daichi — a young son speaking bluntly to his father?

choices.text: 俺 いつでも辞めるから
私はいつでも辞職いたしますので
僕、いつでも退社させていただきますよ

feedback.correct_en: Daichi uses blunt casual speech (俺, 辞める, から). This matches his rough father-son register throughout the chapter.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is formal business keigo; C mixes humble keigo with 僕 and sounds artificial. Neither fits a son grumbling at home.

prompt.context_jp: 大橋への決意表明。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Miyazawa's firm declaration?

choices.text: 私は マラソン足袋の開発を続けます
マラソン足袋の開発は 私が続けますを
続けます 私は マラソン足袋の開発

feedback.correct_en: Standard SOV order with topic-は + object-を + verb. Clean, resolute — matches a formal declaration.
feedback.incorrect_en: B scrambles particles (を after 続けます is ungrammatical); C's inverted order feels unnatural for a solemn committed statement.

contrast_examples.en: It's I who will continue the work (focus-inverted, marked).

prompt.context_jp: 宮沢が大橋に食い下がる場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits a company president challenging a bank officer with controlled anger?

choices.text: あなた 一度でも うちの足袋を 履いたことがありますか
お前さ、一回でもうちの足袋履いたことある？
貴殿におかれましては 弊社の足袋を ご着用賜りましたでしょうか

feedback.correct_en: あなた + plain polite question hits the right register: firm, pointed, but still 社長-to-outsider level. Matches the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's お前 + タメ口 is too rude for a business setting; C's over-formal keigo would blunt the confrontational edge.

contrast_examples.jp: ございますでしょうか？

prompt.context_jp: あけみが職人たちを叱咤する——
prompt.prompt_en: Which fits Akemi's rough, no-nonsense style with the workshop crew?

choices.text: みんな 何 サボってんの！ さっさと本業の足袋のノルマ 終わらせて
皆様、何をなさっておられるのですか。至急、業務をお進めください
皆さん、どうしてお手を止めていらっしゃるの？ ご本業を優先してね

feedback.correct_en: Akemi uses blunt, familiar scolding (サボってんの, さっさと) consistent with her role as the plain-speaking matriarch of the shop.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is office-formal keigo — totally wrong for shouting at longtime craftsmen; C's soft-polite 'manager mom' tone doesn't match her sharp edge.
